# windows_network_adapters (Data Source)

Reads the network adapter inventory of the remote Windows host without managing it. This is a **standalone collection** data source — no sibling resource exists.

Optional filters narrow the result: `names` (exact, case-insensitive), `name_regex` (RE2 match on the adapter name), `mac_address` (any common spelling), `status` (`Up`, `Disconnected`, `Disabled` or `NotPresent`, case-insensitive), `physical_only` (pass `-Physical` to `Get-NetAdapter`) and `include_hidden` (pass `-IncludeHidden`). Omitted filters match everything.

`adapters` carries one object per matching adapter, sorted by `interface_index`; an empty match is a valid empty list, never an error. `is_management` marks the adapter owning the address of the current SSH session (advisory inventory; never asserted in automation because it is host-dependent). Unbound MTUs report `null` (the host has no family address to size); unreported strings report `""`.

The Terraform data source ID is the hex SHA-256 of the normalised filter set.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    windows = {
      source  = "kfrlabs/windows"
      version = "~> 0.1"
    }
  }
}

provider "windows" {
  host     = var.windows_host
  username = var.windows_username
  password = var.windows_password
}

# All physical, visible adapters that are up.
data "windows_network_adapters" "physical_up" {
  physical_only = true
  status        = "Up"
}

output "adapter_names" {
  value       = [for a in data.windows_network_adapters.physical_up.adapters : a.name]
  description = "Names of the physical adapters that are up."
}

locals {
  # Never place the storage address on the management NIC.
  storage_nic = [
    for a in data.windows_network_adapters.physical_up.adapters :
    a if !a.is_management
  ][0]
}

resource "windows_net_ip_address" "storage" {
  interface_alias = local.storage_nic.name
  ip_address      = "198.51.100.10"
  prefix_length   = 24
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `include_hidden` (Boolean) Pass -IncludeHidden to Get-NetAdapter. Omit (null) means false.
- `mac_address` (String) Restrict the result to the adapter with this MAC address, in any common spelling (colons, dashes, dots, any case).
- `name_regex` (String) Restrict the result to adapter names matching this RE2 regular expression.
- `names` (Set of String) Restrict the result to these adapter names (exact, case-insensitive). Omit to match every name.
- `physical_only` (Boolean) Pass -Physical to Get-NetAdapter. Omit (null) means false.
- `status` (String) Restrict the result to one adapter status: Up, Disconnected, Disabled or NotPresent (case-insensitive).
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `adapters` (Attributes List) Matching adapters, sorted by interface_index. Empty when no adapter matches the filters. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--adapters))
- `id` (String) Data source ID; hex SHA-256 of the normalised filter set (sorted lower-case names, regex, normalised MAC, upper-case status, bools).

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).


<a id="nestedatt--adapters"></a>
### Nested Schema for `adapters`

Read-Only:

- `admin_enabled` (Boolean) True unless the adapter AdminStatus is Down.
- `default_gateways` (List of String) Default-route next hops covering this interface, sorted.
- `dhcp_enabled` (Boolean) True when DHCP is enabled on the IPv4 interface.
- `dns_servers` (List of String) Effective DNS servers for this interface, sorted.
- `driver_description` (String) Driver description; empty when unreported.
- `driver_provider` (String) Driver provider; empty when unreported.
- `driver_version` (String) Driver version; empty when unreported.
- `interface_description` (String) Driver description string, as observed on the host.
- `interface_index` (Number) Numeric interface index, as observed on the host.
- `ipv4_addresses` (List of String) Bound IPv4 addresses in canonical CIDR form, sorted.
- `ipv6_addresses` (List of String) Bound IPv6 addresses in canonical CIDR form (link-local kept), sorted.
- `is_management` (Boolean) True when this adapter owns the address of the current SSH session (advisory; never assert it in automation).
- `is_physical` (Boolean) True for physical adapters (negation of the host Virtual flag).
- `is_virtual` (Boolean) Host-reported Virtual flag.
- `link_speed_bps` (Number) Receive link speed in bits per second; 0 when unknown or disconnected.
- `mac_address` (String) Adapter MAC in lower aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff form; empty when the host reports none.
- `media_type` (String) NdisMedium mapped to its documented name (e.g. 802.3); empty when unknown.
- `mtu_ipv4` (Number) IPv4 NlMtu; null when the family is unbound on the interface.
- `mtu_ipv6` (Number) IPv6 NlMtu; null when the family is unbound on the interface.
- `name` (String) Adapter friendly name, as observed on the host.
- `network_category` (String) Connection-profile category; empty when the interface has no profile.
- `physical_media_type` (String) NdisPhysicalMedium mapped to its documented name (e.g. 802.3); empty when unknown.
- `status` (String) Derived adapter status: Up, Disconnected, Disabled or NotPresent.
- `vlan_id` (Number) Adapter VLAN ID; 0 when untagged or unreported.
